slot.brief: Figure shows a haloalkane substrate; sequence: alcoholic KOH (E2), then HBr addition (Markovnikov), then aqueous KOH substitution; ask for the final product structure.

stem: Following E2 elimination with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ ($\Delta$), HBr addition, and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ substitution, what is the final product from the haloalkane shown in the figure?

verdicts.working: The haloalkane is 1-bromo-2-methylpropane. E2 elimination gives 2-methylpropene; HBr addition gives 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, and aqueous KOH substitution gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

working:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br}\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH},\ \Delta}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C{=}CH}_2$$
$$\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}\xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH}}(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$$

Independent check: The haloalkane is 1-bromo-2-methylpropane. E2 elimination gives 2-methylpropene; HBr addition gives 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, and aqueous KOH substitution gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH and heat cause E2 elimination; HBr then adds to the alkene in Markovnikov fashion, followed by substitution with aqueous KOH.
$$ (CH_3)_2CHCH_2Br \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH},\ \Delta} (CH_3)_2C{=}CH_2 \xrightarrow{HBr} (CH_3)_3CBr \xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH}} (CH_3)_3COH $$
The final product is 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
